why: Doc sentence verified verbatim at line 767 of the curl'd page (whole line read; the surrounding troubleshooting block does not reverse it). The cited repo facts are all accurate: grep -ac enableFileCheckpointing packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts -> 0 (the file really does carry NUL bytes, so -a mattered), grep -ac rewindFiles -> 0, the SDK Options literal opens at claude-agent.ts:1213 and never names either symbol, file-checkpoints.ts:571 is createFileCheckpoint, and its only two non-test callers are packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1644 and packages/shared/src/agent/backend/nestor-cloud/tool-executor.ts:155. The finding is still refuted on two independent grounds. (1) WRONG CONTRACT / WRONG SUBSYSTEM. The quoted sentence governs the SDK's own rewind API - Query.rewindFiles() and claude -p --rewind-files - and the 'File rewinding is not enabled' error they raise. Nessy never calls that API (rewindFiles occurs 0 times repo-wide outside docs). Nessy's rewind is an independent engine: revertFileCheckpoint / rewindToMessage (SessionManager.ts:13687, :13776) read OUR manifest at <sessionPath>/file_checkpoints/, never the SDK store. So the missing option is not the cause of an empty Claude rewind, and setting it would not change one observable byte - it would populate a store no Nessy code reads. This is trap #3 from inert-worklist section 4 in its causal form: the identifier really is unwired, but the stated causal chain is false. (2) DATED RECORDED DECISION WITH A WRITTEN REASON - not one of the nine in inert-worklist section 3, but a plan-level one, which AGENTS.md treats as exactly the same kind of artifact ('A plan is where a deviation's reason lives'). docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-25-claude-backend-turn-contract.md Task 6 ran this precise investigation and concluded 'Scope chosen: none. Stopping and reporting, per the plan's stop condition,' naming two blockers that make Query.rewindFiles() unreachable: claude-agent.ts:2345 nulls this.currentQuery in chatImpl's finally while rewind is a between-turns action after strictDrainSessionForMutation, so no subprocess exists to receive the SDKControlRewindFilesRequest; and rewindFiles takes an SDK user-message UUID that nothing on the Claude path captures. The plan then lists 'Setting enableFileCheckpointing: true on its own' as deliberately NOT done, because with no reachable caller it is a speculative unused option. docs/architecture/file-checkpoint-rewind.md:124 and :130 carry the same verdict as shipped architecture record. The underlying product gap is real but is already an open, tracked row, not a new divergence: 2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md P4 (Tier 2), which also corrects the harm this finding inherits - the SDK store lands in ~/.claude/file-history/, not the working dir.
correctedState: Nessy does not use the Claude Agent SDK's file-checkpointing or its rewindFiles() control request at all; both identifiers are absent from claude-agent.ts and from the whole repo outside docs. Rewind on every backend is served by Nessy's own engine (packages/shared/src/sessions/file-checkpoints.ts), driven from two dispatch sites - Pi's tool executor (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1644) and the Nestor Cloud tool executor (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/nestor-cloud/tool-executor.ts:155) - where checkpointing is unconditional rather than opt-in, so this page's per-session enable option has no Nessy counterpart to be missing. The genuine consequence, already recorded and open, is narrower than the finding states and is not caused by the missing option: because a Claude-backend session's Write/Edit/NotebookEdit run inside the SDK subprocess, our beforeDispatch never fires, so no entries exist in <sessionPath>/file_checkpoints/. rewindToMessage({restoreFiles:true}) then truncates the transcript and returns success with restoredCheckpoints: 0, and the ungated 'Revert last file edit' menu item (SessionMenu.tsx:237) returns 'No file checkpoint found'. Passing enableFileCheckpointing would not fix either surface; docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-25-claude-backend-turn-contract.md Task 6 records the decision to leave it unset and names the two blockers (no live query handle between turns; no SDK user-message UUID) that make the SDK rewind path unreachable. Tracked as 2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md P4 and in docs/architecture/file-checkpoint-rewind.md.
